newsitem.title: GREECE: EXPLOSION ROCKS ATHENS SCHOOL, NONE REPORTED HURT.
newsitem.headline: EXPLOSION ROCKS ATHENS SCHOOL, NONE REPORTED HURT.

text.p: An explosion rocked the Athens Polytechnic School on Wednesday after someone called a local television station and warned that a bomb was about to go off, Athens Skai television reported.
It said the blast was caused by a timebomb on the second floor of the engineering school in central Athens. There were no reports of injuries.
Police confirmed the explosion was caused by a timebomb and said the advance warning had prevented anyone from being hurt.

The Athens Polytechnic is the scene of clashes between police and hooligans around November 17 every year as Greece prepares to commemorate a student uprising which led to the fall of a 1967-74 military junta.
Skai television said the caller did not claim responsibility on behalf of any particular organisation. --Steve Weeks, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
